question: Where did Jesus first appear to the eleven disciples after the resurrection?
summary: Matthew 28:16 says the eleven met Jesus on a mountain in Galilee — a multi-day journey from the tomb. Mark 16:14, Luke 24:33-37, and John 20:19 all locate the first group appearance to the eleven in a room in Jerusalem, on the day of the resurrection itself. Same scene, two different cities seventy miles apart.

reconcile.connective: Commentators read Matthew's Galilee meeting as a separate, later gathering — not the same scene as the Jerusalem appearances in Mark, Luke, and John.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman calls this a signature contradiction: Matthew sends the eleven to Galilee while Luke and John place their first Jerusalem gathering that same night.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (And Why We Don't Know About Them)
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (New York: HarperOne, 2009); the same discrepancy was pressed in his 2006 debate with William Lane Craig, "Is There Historical Evidence for the Resurrection of Jesus?" (College of the Holy Cross, March 28, 2006)

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's parallel-column table pairs "Christ's first re-appearance in Galilee" (Matt. 28:16, 17) against "At Jerusalem" (Luke 24:33, 36; John 20:19) and answers that Matthew does not deny but simply passes over the earlier appearances, dwelling on the Galilee meeting as one of great importance.

link.title: GotQuestions: Can the various resurrection accounts from the four Gospels be harmonized?
link.note: harmonized timeline places the Jerusalem appearances on resurrection day before the later Galilee gathering and commissioning of Matthew 28:16-20

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: went away into Galilee: not directly, as soon as the women had delivered their message; for Christ appeared to them the same day at Jerusalem; and so he did at the same place that week; see Joh 20:19, but some time, after this they went together into Galilee, according to Christ's direction both before and after his resurrection, Mat 26:32 …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill explicitly separates the Galilee meeting from the same-day Jerusalem appearance recorded in John 20:19, treating Matthew's scene as later and distinct rather than as the same event relocated.
excerpts.source_note_text:
Then the eleven disciples,.... For Judas was not only gone from them, but was dead; so that there were now but eleven of them: went
away into Galilee: not directly, as soon as the women had delivered their message; for Christ appeared to them the same day at Jerusalem; and so he did at the same place that week; see Joh 20:19, but some time, after this they went together into Galilee, according to Christ's direction both before and after his resurrection, Mat 26:32,
into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them; either before his death, or since he was risen; and very likely at one of the above interviews he had with them. This is generally thought to be Mount Tabor; but of this there is no proof, nor certainty: it might be the mountain near Capernaum, on which he taught, Mat 5:1, or that, if not the same with the other, near the sea of Galilee, where Christ fed four thousand with seven loaves, and a few fishes, Mat 15:29. A mountain was appointed for this meeting, both for solitariness and for sight; for here it was he was seen by above five hundred brethren at once, Co1 15:6.
